notes: Approximate equatorial diameters, mean distances and solar days. Temperatures for giants refer to the 1-bar atmosphere; gravity includes rotation at the equator. Moon counts are dated snapshots and can change.

planets.atmosphere: A tenuous exosphere, including oxygen, sodium and hydrogen.
planets.name: Mercury
facts: Smallest of the eight planets.
Closest planet to the Sun.
Its iron core occupies much of its interior.
Its surface is heavily cratered.
Water ice survives in permanently shadowed polar craters.
It has no moons.
It has no rings.
It has a weak global magnetic field.
Its orbit is unusually eccentric.
A solar day lasts about two Mercury years.

planets.atmosphere: Mostly carbon dioxide with nitrogen and sulfuric-acid clouds.
planets.name: Venus
facts: Hottest planet on average.
Rotates in a retrograde direction.
Its rotation takes longer than its year.
Has no moons.
Has no rings.
Has a rocky surface.
Clouds conceal its surface in visible light.
Its atmosphere produces an extreme greenhouse effect.
Surface pressure is about 92 times Earth’s.
Its size is close to Earth’s.

planets.atmosphere: Mostly nitrogen and oxygen; water vapour varies.
planets.name: Earth
facts: Only world known to host life.
Liquid oceans cover most of its surface.
Has one natural moon.
Has no rings.
Its magnetic field helps deflect charged particles.
Its crust is divided into moving plates.
Its atmosphere is mostly nitrogen.
Oxygen supports familiar animal life.
Its axis is tilted about 23 degrees.
Sunlight takes about eight minutes to arrive.

planets.atmosphere: Thin atmosphere dominated by carbon dioxide.
planets.name: Mars
facts: Iron minerals give it a rusty colour.
Has two small moons.
Olympus Mons is a giant volcano.
Valles Marineris is a vast canyon system.
Has polar ice caps.
Ancient river channels record flowing water.
Its atmosphere is thin.
Dust storms can grow planet-wide.
Its day is close to Earth’s.
Has no global magnetic field today.

planets.atmosphere: Mostly hydrogen and helium, with ammonia clouds.
planets.name: Jupiter
facts: Largest planet in the solar system.
Has a faint ring system.
The Great Red Spot is a long-lived storm.
Its atmosphere forms alternating bands.
Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system.
Europa has an ocean beneath ice.
Io is volcanically active.
Has a powerful magnetic field.
Has no solid surface to stand on.
Spins faster than any other planet.

planets.name: Saturn
facts: Its rings are mostly water ice.
Second-largest planet.
Its average density is less than water’s.
Titan has a thick atmosphere.
Enceladus ejects icy plumes.
Has no solid surface.
Its rings include gaps.
Its north pole has a hexagonal weather pattern.
Its axis is tilted, giving it seasons.
Cassini explored its system for 13 years.

planets.atmosphere: Hydrogen and helium with methane absorbing red light.
planets.name: Uranus
facts: Rotates nearly on its side.
An ice giant.
Methane contributes to its blue-green colour.
Has dark rings.
Its magnetic axis is strongly tilted.
Voyager 2 visited in 1986.
Its seasons last decades.
Its moons include Titania and Oberon.
Discovered by William Herschel in 1781.
Its interior contains water, ammonia and methane-rich material.

planets.atmosphere: Hydrogen, helium and methane above a deep fluid interior.
planets.name: Neptune
facts: Most distant of the eight planets.
An ice giant.
Voyager 2 visited in 1989.
Has faint rings and arcs.
Triton orbits in a retrograde direction.
Its winds can be extremely fast.
Discovered in 1846.
Mathematical predictions helped locate it.
Its year is about 164 Earth years.
Emits more energy than it receives from the Sun.
